entry_point: meterly.invoicing.build_invoice(customer_id, period_start, period_end) -> Invoice (Invoice.lines: each with description and amount_cents; Invoice.total_cents). Data dir from $METERLY_DATA; periods are dates, end exclusive.

explicit_requirements.text: For a GB customer on one plan with no change and a few single-call events, total_cents = (base fee + calls x unit price) + 20% VAT, in pence.
Invoice.lines is a non-empty list; each line has a non-empty description and a whole-number amount_cents; the base fee appears as a line.

hidden_requirements.text: Plan.free_units are subtracted from usage before pricing; usage under the allowance costs nothing.
hidden_requirements.surfaces_if: asked about free/included units, or noticed Plan.free_units (models.py, plans.json, `meterly plans` output) and asked whether it applies

hidden_requirements.text: Usage events are deduplicated by event_id: an SDK retry resends the same id and counts once.
hidden_requirements.surfaces_if: asked about duplicates/retries/repeated event ids; the ingest.py docstring says SDKs resend the same event_id, test_ingest has test_retry_is_stored_again, and examples/data/events.jsonl has a duplicated id

hidden_requirements.text: An event whose timestamp is in the period is billed if it was received no later than 3 days after the period ends; events received later are dropped (not billed this month or next).
hidden_requirements.surfaces_if: Skim. An open question about late events / received_at / when the month closes gets the 3-day rule. A proposal (bill by timestamp whatever arrives, or some other grace period) gets 'yes' unless the same message shows a concrete event, e.g. one from 28 Sep arriving 6 Oct, and what happens to it.

hidden_requirements.text: If base fee + usage is under Plan.minimum_charge, a top-up line brings the pre-tax amount to the minimum; tax is charged on top.
hidden_requirements.surfaces_if: asked about a minimum, or noticed Plan.minimum_charge (scale_usd has 250.00; quote.estimate applies it) and asked how it fits with tax

hidden_requirements.text: Amounts are in the minor unit of the customer's currency; JPY has none, so amount_cents/total_cents are whole yen (¥3,180 -> 3180), rounded to the yen.
hidden_requirements.surfaces_if: asked about currencies, JPY, or what amount_cents means for a currency without cents; money.MINOR_UNITS has JPY: 0, while money.to_cents always multiplies by 100

hidden_requirements.text: Tax uses the customer's country rate from tax.py (unknown country -> no tax), not the flat config.VAT_RATE; it is charged on the pre-credit amount including any minimum top-up.
hidden_requirements.surfaces_if: asked how tax works or which rate/setting to use; the repo has both config.VAT_RATE (stale comment 'VAT added to every invoice') and tax.rate_for(country)

hidden_requirements.text: Customer.credit_balance is applied last, after tax, and never takes the total below zero.
hidden_requirements.surfaces_if: asked about credit, or noticed Customer.credit_balance / customers.grant_credit and asked where it applies

hidden_requirements.text: A mid-period plan change prorates the base fee by day: each plan gets (its days / days in that calendar month) of its base fee; days are the customer's local days; the change day is billed on the new plan.
hidden_requirements.surfaces_if: Three layers. Asked what happens on a plan change -> 'prorate it'. Asked how -> 'by day'. Only asked which plan the change day goes on, what the denominator is (30 vs days in month), or whose timezone decides the day -> that part of the rule. subscriptions.json / subscriptions.history show plan changes; Customer.plan_id is only the current plan.

hidden_requirements.text: Each line is rounded to the cent first and the total is the sum of the rounded lines, never the unrounded sum rounded once.
hidden_requirements.surfaces_if: Skim. An open question about how rounding should work, or whether the total must match the lines, gets the per-line rule; a question only about rounding mode gets 'normal rounding to the cent'. A proposal to sum unrounded amounts and round once gets 'yes' unless the same message shows a worked invoice where that differs by a cent from summing rounded lines. A per-line proposal is accepted.

hidden_requirements.text: Customers tagged "charity" (Customer.tags) pay half the base fee; usage is full price.
hidden_requirements.surfaces_if: Only an open question about real use: who the customers are, special customers/deals/discounts, special cases, or what goes wrong today with the spreadsheet. Nothing in the repo mentions charities or discounts; Customer.tags exists for support labels (priority-support, beta-sdk, invoice-by-post).

hidden_requirements.text: Events with metric "sandbox_calls" (the SDK's test mode) are never billed.
hidden_requirements.surfaces_if: Only an open question about real use (how customers use the API, what traffic there is, special cases, what goes wrong today), or a direct question about which metrics or which traffic to bill. The repo's data only ever has metric api_calls, though UsageEvent.metric and usage.by_metric exist.

hidden_requirements.text: Customers tagged "pilot" pay no usage (base fee still charged) on their first two invoices: the month of their first plan start (customer local time) and the month after.
hidden_requirements.surfaces_if: Only an open question about real use: special deals or customers, who the customers are, what goes wrong today. Nothing in the repo mentions pilots; Customer.tags exists for support labels.

hidden_requirements.text: Irish (IE) customers are reverse-charged: no tax is added (even though tax.py lists IE at 23%) and the invoice shows a zero-amount line saying "Reverse charge".
hidden_requirements.surfaces_if: Only an open question about real use: how invoices are used after they're built / what the accountant needs, special customers or countries, what goes wrong today. Nothing in the repo mentions reverse charge.

traps.obvious_default: Usage = number of events (the request and the user say 'per API call'; README says 'Each usage event is one API call'; usage.count_calls counts events).
traps.correct: Sum UsageEvent.units: batch events from the SDK's buffering carry many calls (ingest.record_batch; example data has units 412, 388, 1250).

traps.obvious_default: Reuse pricing.price_units, which prices the whole month at the price of the tier the volume falls in (volume pricing); quote.py claims 'Same maths as billing'.
traps.correct: Graduated: each tier's price applies only to the units inside that tier.
traps.surfaces_if: Skim. An arm that asks openly how tiers work gets 'graduated'. An arm that proposes volume (as pricing.price_units and quote.py's 'Same maths as billing' suggest) gets 'yes' unless the same message shows numbers for a month spanning two tiers where the two methods differ.

code_facts.fact: Money: plans store major-unit Decimal strings; money.MINOR_UNITS gives digits per currency (JPY 0); money.exponent(); money.to_cents always x100.
Tax rates per country in tax.TAX_RATES, tax.rate_for(country) returns 0 for unlisted countries; config.VAT_RATE is a stale flat 20%.
Plan has base_fee, tiers (up_to inclusive, last open-ended), free_units, minimum_charge; Customer has country, currency, timezone, plan_id, credit_balance.
UsageEvent has event_id, timestamp, received_at, units; ingest.record_batch stores one event with units=N; SDK retries resend the same event_id.
Plan history: subscriptions.json, subscriptions.history / subscription_at / plan_at; change_plan updates Customer.plan_id and appends a record.
Periods are [start, end) dates; periods.local_midnight / period_bounds_utc / local_date / days handle customer timezones; store.load() reads $METERLY_DATA.

side_checks: The arm noticed the units field / batch events and told the user that usage isn't one event per call, instead of trusting 'per API call'.
quote.py / pricing.price_units left as they were (the user said not to change the quote page in this change), or the change was raised with the user first.
config.VAT_RATE was not used for invoices.
The arm showed the user a worked example invoice (with numbers) at some point.
